newsitem.title: ITALY: Brcko gets international supervision until 1998.
newsitem.headline: Brcko gets international supervision until 1998.

text.p: A U.S. arbiter decided on Friday the hotly disputed, strategic northern Bosnian town of Brcko would be placed under international supervision pending a final ruling on its future next year.

"No winner is being announced today...We want international supervision for Brcko for not less than one year...to allow for a reduction of tensions. We will make a final choice no later than March 1998," Roberts Owen said.

"This firmly rejects the status quo in favour of a major international effort to reduce the underlying tensions in the area," he told a news conference after talks with the international community's High Representative for Bosnia, Carl Bildt.
"We are not yet convinced that any of the three candidates are sufficiently stabilised to take on the situation," Owen said.
"It is very possible that the outcome could be that Brcko could become a special district of Bosnia-Herzegovina, along the lines of Washington DC."
Owen, who announced the decision at the Italian Foreign Ministry in Rome, headed an arbitration panel on which he was flanked by a Bosnian Serb and a member from the Moslem-Croat federation.
"It's definitely enough to avoid war," U.S. Assistant Secretary of State John Kornblum told Reuters at the ministry.

"This is the mother of all difficulties in the Bosnian peace process," Bildt said. "Everyone wants to have 100 percent but that is not possible so it's an attempt by the arbitration tribunal...to strike a balance and to deal with the underlying forces of the conflict."
The tribunal's arbitration statement said it would be "inappropriate" to decide "final allocation of political reponsibility" in the area at this time.

"The Inter-Entity Boundary Line in the region will remain unchanged and the tribunal shall continue to monitor the situation in the area during the period of interim international supervision," the statement said.

Brcko, which lies on the Sava River, is in a narrow land corridor linking eastern and western halves of Serb-controlled territory in northern Bosnia. It was seized by the Bosnian Serbs early in the 1992-95 war.
The dispute over who should control it almost caused the collapse of talks to end the conflict in late 1995.

The panel had been due to rule by mid-December but the deadline for settling the dispute was extended until February 15. Serb and Moslem delegations presented their arguments during 10 days of arbitration hearings in Rome last month.
Moslem leaders have said Brcko should be awarded to the federation based on the pre-war population in which Moslems and Croats formed a majority.
They argued that giving the town to the Serbs would reward ethnic expulsions carried out when Serb forces captured the area in May 1992.
The Bosnian Serbs have insisted the town must be kept under Serb control or Serb territory would be cut in half . They have threatened to go to war over the issue.
